title: Apex security: sharing, CRUD, FLS, user mode, and safe dynamic queries
objectives: Separate sharing (which records) from CRUD/FLS (which objects and fields) and from authentication.
Choose with sharing, without sharing, or inherited sharing and explain the default when omitted.
Use USER_MODE / AccessLevel.USER_MODE or stripInaccessible / SECURITY_ENFORCED as cited—not as folklore.
Bind dynamic SOQL and refuse string-concatenated user input.
diagnostic_question: A REST class omitted a sharing keyword, builds SOQL by concatenating a filter string, and updates Amount. A standard user can see every Account and overwrite a hidden field. What is sharing vs CRUD vs FLS vs user mode vs safe dynamic queries?
definition: Apex security is several layers. Sharing keywords decide whether the class honors the running user's record sharing. CRUD is object create/read/update/delete permission; FLS is field permission. User mode (WITH USER_MODE / as user / AccessLevel.USER_MODE) asks the platform to enforce sharing, CRUD, and FLS together. Dynamic SOQL is safe only with binds or escapeSingleQuotes—not concatenated filters. ([Enforcing Sharing Rules](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_keywords_sharing.htm); [Enforcing Object and Field Permissions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_security_sharing_rules.htm); [Apex Developer Guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_dev_guide.htm))
why_it_matters: Default Apex is system mode for object/field permissions. Interviewers fail candidates who say with sharing 'does FLS' or who concatenate SOQL. User mode is the modern way to run as the user without a pile of manual checks.
sixty_second_explanation: Hotel keys: sharing is which rooms your floor key opens; CRUD is whether you may enter the room at all; FLS is the minibar and safe. User mode is walking the hall as a guest; omitted sharing plus system DML is the night manager's master key. inherited sharing takes the caller's key. Dynamic SOQL is the front-desk log: bind the guest name, never glue their raw string into the query. with sharing is not FLS. Profiles are not authentication (SEC-001).
deeper_explanation: with sharing enforces record-level sharing for that class. without sharing ignores sharing (still not a CRUD/FLS grant by itself). inherited sharing uses the caller’s mode—recommended for entry-agnostic services. If you omit the keyword, the class does not enforce sharing unless a caller’s with sharing context applies in documented inherited cases—re-read the sharing-keywords page for the API version; do not invent a 'default with sharing' story. ([Sharing keywords](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_keywords_sharing.htm))

CRUD and FLS are permission-set/profile capabilities on objects and fields. System-mode Apex can read and write fields the user cannot see. WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED on SOQL fails the query if FLS/CRUD would hide fields. Security.stripInaccessible removes inaccessible fields from queries/DML. Schema describe checks are the older manual path. ([Object and Field Permissions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_security_sharing_rules.htm))

User mode (WITH USER_MODE in SOQL, insert/update as user, AccessLevel.USER_MODE on Database methods) enforces sharing, CRUD, and FLS in one declaration. It is not the same as with sharing alone. Reverify exact exception types on the current user-mode page rather than inventing error names.

Dynamic SOQL: Database.query with bind variables (queryWithBinds / :bind in string where supported) or String.escapeSingleQuotes. Never concatenate unsanitized request parameters into WHERE. Dynamic SOQL still consumes SOQL governors (APEX-007). USER_MODE or SECURITY_ENFORCED still apply to the string you built.
Scheduled Apex runs as system (APEX-011). That does not excuse without sharing on a user-facing REST class. global APIs (APEX-001) widen who can call the class; they do not replace FLS.

mental_model.analogy: A hotel key cabinet: sharing is the floor key (which rooms), CRUD is whether you may open the door, FLS is the minibar and in-room safe, user mode is walking as a guest, system mode is the night manager's master, and dynamic SOQL is the guest-name log you must bind not glue.
useful_mapping: floor key → with sharing / record visibility
door permission → CRUD on the object
night manager → system-mode Apex without user-mode DML
inherit the caller's key → inherited sharing
bind the guest name → bind variables / queryWithBinds
glued hallway rumor → concatenated SOQL injection
where_it_breaks: with sharing does not hide fields; FLS/user mode does.
stripInaccessible does not replace sharing by itself.
The hotel analogy does not encode OWD math (later SEC topics).

  Req[User or integration request] --> Auth[Authentication: not this lesson]

flowchart TD
  Need[Need Apex to honor the user?] --> Q1{Record visibility?}
  Q1 -->|Yes| Share[with sharing or inherited sharing]
  Q1 -->|Must see all rows by design| Without[without sharing plus a written reason]
  Need --> Q2{Object and field permissions?}

claims.claim: with sharing, without sharing, and inherited sharing control whether the class enforces the running user's record sharing. inherited sharing follows the caller.
System-mode Apex does not automatically enforce CRUD/FLS. Documented tools include WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED, Security.stripInaccessible, and Schema describe checks.
User mode (WITH USER_MODE / as user / AccessLevel.USER_MODE) is the Guide's way to enforce user sharing and object/field permissions together. Confirm syntax on the current TOC.
Dynamic SOQL must use binds or escapeSingleQuotes; concatenated user input is unsafe. Those queries still count toward SOQL governors (100/200).

changed_in_release: User-mode SOQL/DML syntax expanded in recent API versions. Reverify WITH USER_MODE and as user on the Summer '26 Guide TOC for the class API version.
unresolved_uncertainty: Exact exception type when USER_MODE DML fails FLS should be read from the current user-mode page.
Omit-keyword default interaction with inherited sharing inner classes: re-read sharing keywords rather than inventing.

telugu_glossary.telugu: అతిథిగా నడవడం: sharing + CRUD + FLS కలిసి.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Sharing is which records. CRUD is the object. FLS is the field. User mode enforces all three. with sharing is not FLS. Dynamic SOQL uses binds, never glued strings. Default Apex is system mode for permissions.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I pick inherited sharing on reusable services so the entry class decides. User-facing REST uses with sharing plus USER_MODE DML. I use SECURITY_ENFORCED when a hidden field must fail the query, stripInaccessible when I should drop fields and continue. I bind dynamic filters. I never say sharing 'does FLS.' I cite the sharing-keywords and object-permissions Guide topics, not a blog checklist.

terminology.plain: Whether this class honors record sharing.
terminology.precise: with sharing, without sharing, inherited sharing on the class definition.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: OWD: org-wide default, not an Apex keyword.

terminology.precise: Checked via user mode, SECURITY_ENFORCED, stripInaccessible, or describe. Not automatic in system-mode Apex.
terminology.example: User cannot create LAB_Invoice__c; user-mode insert fails.
terminology.boundary: Scheduled Apex running as system still needs an explicit story.

terminology.precise: Which fields the user may read or edit. System-mode Apex can ignore it unless you enforce.
terminology.example: stripInaccessible removes Amount__c from a queried LAB_ row.
terminology.boundary: SECURITY_ENFORCED fails the query rather than stripping.

terminology.plain: Run SOQL/DML as the user, enforcing sharing + CRUD + FLS.
terminology.precise: WITH USER_MODE, as user, AccessLevel.USER_MODE. Confirm current syntax in the Guide TOC.
terminology.non_example: with sharing alone on a class that still does system DML.

terminology.plain: SOQL built at runtime as a string.
terminology.precise: Safe with binds / queryWithBinds / escapeSingleQuotes. Unsafe with concatenated request parameters.
terminology.example: Database.queryWithBinds('SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name = :n', binds, AccessLevel.USER_MODE)
terminology.non_example: Static [SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name = :name].
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Dynamic DML (sObject type chosen at runtime).

terminology.plain: SOQL clause that fails closed on inaccessible fields/objects.
terminology.precise: Query throws if CRUD/FLS would hide selected fields.
terminology.example: SELECT Amount__c FROM LAB_Invoice__c WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED

terminology.plain: Security method that removes inaccessible fields from in-memory sObjects.
terminology.precise: Use before returning data or performing DML so hidden fields are not read or written.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Schema describe isAccessible loops (older manual path).
terminology.boundary: Does not bind dynamic SOQL for you.

terminology.precise: Service classes that should not hard-code with/without.
terminology.boundary: Entry class still chooses with or without.

when_to_use: When user-facing Apex must honor sharing: with sharing or inherited sharing, not an omitted keyword.
When the user must not read or write hidden fields: user mode, SECURITY_ENFORCED, or stripInaccessible—not with sharing alone.
When CRUD on LAB_Invoice__c is missing: user-mode DML should fail rather than insert as system.
When filters come from the client: safe dynamic queries with binds, never concatenated SOQL.
When a batch must see all rows: without sharing plus a comment, then still decide CRUD/FLS.
When an interviewer conflates authentication with Apex security layers.
when_not_to_use: Do not treat with sharing as FLS or CRUD.
Do not use without sharing on a REST/UI class 'for convenience'.
Do not concatenate request parameters into dynamic SOQL.
Do not invent a numeric 'security governor'; cite SOQL 100/200 only as query budget.
Do not confuse profile CRUD with authentication (SEC-001).
Do not skip standard-user tests because admin tests were green.
configuration_or_code_location: Class header: with sharing / without sharing / inherited sharing.
SOQL: WITH USER_MODE or WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED; DML: as user / AccessLevel.USER_MODE.
Security.stripInaccessible in a service before returning rows to LWC.
Permission sets on the LAB_ test user, not View All Data.

interview_questions.question: Sharing vs CRUD vs FLS vs user mode?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Sharing is which records. CRUD is the object. FLS is the field. User mode enforces all three. with sharing is not FLS. Default Apex is system mode for permissions.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I draw four boxes. I put inherited sharing on services. I pick USER_MODE for user-facing DML. I mention SECURITY_ENFORCED vs stripInaccessible. I refuse to call this authentication. I cite the sharing-keywords and object-permissions Guide topics.
interview_questions.example: Standard user querying LAB_Invoice__c: fewer rows (sharing), no Amount__c (FLS), cannot insert if CRUD missing (user mode).
follow_ups: What if the keyword is omitted?

interview_questions.question: How do you write safe dynamic queries?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Binds or queryWithBinds, optional USER_MODE. Never concatenate request parameters. escapeSingleQuotes if you must build a string. Still counts as SOQL toward 100/200.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I allowlist field names if the client chooses a field. I show a broken concat and the bind fix. I add a test with a quote-injection payload. I do not claim dynamic SOQL is banned—only unsafe construction is.
interview_questions.example: Database.queryWithBinds('SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name = :n', map, AccessLevel.USER_MODE)

interview_questions.question: LWC shows Amount__c to a user whose FLS hides it. Walk the diagnosis.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The Apex is system mode and selected the field. with sharing would not hide it. Add USER_MODE or stripInaccessible or stop selecting the field.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I check the class keyword, the SOQL, DTOs, and @AuraEnabled cache. I runAs the standard user. I do not change OWD to 'fix FLS.' I mention inner classes can drop inherited sharing if declared without sharing.
interview_questions.example: LAB_InvoiceService system query includes Amount__c and returns it to the wire.
follow_ups: Does Lightning Data Service honor FLS?

interview_questions.question: A managed Batch uses without sharing; a new REST class copied that header. Risk?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: REST now ignores sharing. Users see every LAB_ row. Batch may still be justified; REST is not. Use inherited sharing on the service and with sharing on REST.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat without sharing as a privileged annotation requiring a comment. I add runAs tests on the REST path. I do not 'fix' it by adding SECURITY_ENFORCED only—rows would still be the wrong set if sharing is off and user mode is off.
tradeoffs: inherited sharing as the default service
follow_ups: What about Queueable called from REST?

interview_questions.question: When do you choose SECURITY_ENFORCED versus stripInaccessible versus user-mode DML?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: SECURITY_ENFORCED when a hidden selected field must fail the query. stripInaccessible when you drop fields and continue. User-mode DML when inserts/updates must honor CRUD/FLS/sharing together.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I often use user mode as the default for new user-facing code. I use SECURITY_ENFORCED on reporting queries that must not silently omit columns. I use stripInaccessible when building a DTO for LWC from a system query I cannot yet migrate. I reverify syntax on the current Guide.
interview_questions.example: Reporting query WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED; LWC mapper uses stripInaccessible during migration.
weak_answer_warnings: Using all three on one line without a reason

interview_questions.question: Standard user gets zero rows; admin gets hundreds. Is it a bug?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Maybe not: with sharing or user mode is working. Confirm OWD, sharing rules, and whether the business wanted that. If the user should see more, fix sharing metadata, not the keyword.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I compare runAs results, role, and permission sets. I do not flip to without sharing to 'make the demo work.' I check if USER_MODE also hid rows the user cannot CRUD.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ invoices private OWD; standard user owns none.
follow_ups: Does inherited sharing from a without-sharing caller leak?
weak_answer_warnings: Removing with sharing to unblock UAT

interview_questions.question: How do you test Apex security without SeeAllData?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Insert LAB_ rows as the test, create a standard user, assign a permission set, System.runAs, assert row counts and field absence. Isolation is APEX-016; the assertions are this lesson.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I never query production Accounts to prove FLS. I create two invoices with different owners. I hide Amount__c on the perm set. I assert query size 1 and Amount__c not returned. I add an injection string test.
interview_questions.example: runAs(standard) on LAB_InvoiceService.listMine() expects one row and no Amount__c.
follow_ups: Can you runAs a guest user?
weak_answer_warnings: SeeAllData to grab a real user

interview_questions.question: Where does Apex security stop and platform sharing start?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Apex keywords and user mode enforce whatever sharing metadata exists. They do not create OWD, roles, or sharing rules. Wrong OWD cannot be 'fixed' with USER_MODE.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I send OWD/role/workbench questions to the SEC track. I still own the class keyword, FLS enforcement, and binds. Interviewers like that split. I mention scheduled/system context as a reason privileged jobs exist.
interview_questions.example: Private OWD plus with sharing: users see what sharing grants; Apex does not invent extra rows.
weak_answer_warnings: Claiming with sharing creates sharing rules
